text.title: Architectural Impact PR Ranking — Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete Monday report over three repositories, with a note on every value a reader might question, and one report from the same week as first generated that breaks seven subject rules and what the validator and the architect say about it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Three repositories, 143 PRs opened or merged in the week, a 45-minute Monday slot. The first ranker read PR titles and put "BREAKING: rename test helper" on top while a "small refactor" that touched the OpenAPI contract sat at rank 9. The tech lead runs steps 1-9 of `content/04-procedure.xml` and produces the report below for week 37.

example.title: Four ranked PRs that fit the slot, one deferred, one merged without review
example.note: `acme/orders#4412` ranks first with `title_context` "small refactor of order status": the diff touched three contract files and two public API paths, and the title never entered the score. `acme/orders#4398`, titled "BREAKING", ranks third on its diff alone.

`acme/billing#902` scores `dependency_changes` 3.0 because it adds one new dependency (weight 3.0); the 31 Renovate patch-bump PRs are in `exclusions.bot_authors` and would have scored 0.1 each if ranked.

`acme/payments` has `has_public_api_list` false, so `acme/payments#77` carries `public_api_delta` 0 even though it is a migration; the report prints "no API surface list" for that repo until the list lands (the decision tree's conclusion for this week).
`top_n` is 4 with `summed_read_minutes` 41 against a 45-minute box; `acme/orders#4405` scored above threshold but would take 36 minutes, so it is deferred with its score rather than dropped.
4 ranked + 1 deferred + 31 + 2 + 17 + 4 + 84 below threshold = 143, the population total; the reader can tell "scored low" from "never scanned".

`acme/billing#899` merged on Thursday night above threshold and appears in `merged_without_review` with the merger's handle; last week's precision is 3 of 4, and `weights_changed` is false so no `weight_change` block is present.

section.title: Bad example: the same week from the first ranker

example.title: Seven subject rules broken
example.note: What the validator prints: `window.state_filter: 'open-only' is not the required const` (r-window-repos-exclusions-stated, fm-merged-before-session-invisible); `repositories[0]: missing required field: public_api_paths_config` (r-public-api-surface-enumerated-per-repo); `weights: missing required field: infra_or_config_changes` (r-score-formula-published-in-report); `dependency_kind_weights.patch_bump: 1.0 is above maximum 0.5` and `lockfile_only: 1.0 is not the required const 0` (r-dependency-change-weighted-by-kind); `signals_from_diff_only: False is not the required const True` (r-signals-from-diff-not-metadata); `ranked[0]: missing required field: outcome` and `ranked[1]: missing required field: changed_lines` and `read_minutes` (r-top-n-fits-the-session, r-precision-recorded-per-session); `<root>: missing required field: merged_without_review` (r-merged-without-review-flagged); `weight_change.precision_weeks_cited: 1 is below minimum 4` and `precision_values: 1 items is under minItems 4` (r-precision-recorded-per-session).

What the architect sees beyond the validator: `summed_read_minutes` 190 for a 45-minute box means the bottom eight PRs get a glance (fm-top-n-exceeds-session); `bot_authors` is 0 while 31 Renovate PRs were in the week, so the totals cannot reconcile; and the rename of a test helper scores 30 while the contract change scores 12, the signature of fm-title-driven-score. The report goes back to step 1.

list.item: Print the signals, not just the score: the moment a reader can recompute rank 1 from the table, the argument about weights becomes an argument about evidence.
Reconciliation is the audit: a population total the exclusions do not sum to is how a merged contract change disappears.
Precision is cheap to record and expensive to reconstruct; four hit-or-miss marks a week is the whole cost of being allowed to tune the weights.
